properties.description: The Republic Hotel is a historic URM building in the International Special Review District. It is a mixed-use retail and 100% Affordable Housing project that is on the Priority 2 list. The scope of work includes voluntary full seismic upgrades, masonry restoration, window replacement and restoration, adding an elevator, new roofing, and adding a 5th floor penthouse floor. Mechanical and electrical upgrades include new exhaust fans, new heat pumps for heating and cooling, low flow plumbing fixtures, new all building hot and cold water plumbing system, all LED lighting, a new fire sprinkler system, a new fire alarm system. Interior improvements include new cabinets and counter tops, Energy Star appliances, tubs/showers, new flooring, base, and paint throughout. cold shell for the commercial spaces. All new insulation on entire exterior envelope as part of the work. We are looking at 36 family sized units over retail/restaurant space.

properties.description:
Cascade Public Media (CPM), a prominent local media organization, is embarking on an exciting venture as they relocate to their new headquarters located at 316 Broadway. This building was originally constructed by Childhaven, a school dedicated to nurturing young minds. The property is currently zoned as MR(M), which imposes certain restrictions on signage, particularly limiting them to a maximum height of 15 feet. However, with CPM's vision for the building, the team is keen to explore the possibility of obtaining a zoning variance that would enable the installation of a distinctive wall sign on the south-facing upper story of this impressive 5-story structure.

The decision to seek a zoning variance for signage is driven by the building's transformation into a commercial office space, complete with a first-floor event area. This shift in function and the building's importance within the community make it essential for CPM to align its signage with its new role effectively. To accomplish this, CPM is aiming to have its signage proposal reviewed under the NC3 sign code. The NC3 zoning classification is well-suited for properties in the surrounding area and has the flexibility needed to accommodate signage that complements the building's use as both a commercial office space and a venue for community events.

By pursuing this zoning variance and aligning their signage with the NC3 code, CPM demonstrates their commitment to both preserving the building's historical significance and adapting it to serve the evolving needs of the community. This move not only reflects CPM's dedication to their mission but also underscores their desire to create a welcoming and distinctive presence in the heart of the community while respecting the building's storied past.

properties.description:
The Argosy float replacement project is intended to address the maintenance needs of a small existing float at Seattle's Pier 54, which has reached the end of its useful life. This float provides one of two downtown boarding locations for Argosy, making it a key component of Argosy's commercial tour operation. The float is also used for short-term moorage of maintenance and assist vessels. An in-kind replacement is needed; refer to the attached photographs of the existing, deteriorating float.
 
The project proposes to remove the existing float in its entirety. The float will be detached from its support piles and disposed of off-site. Thereafter, a prefabricated float will be delivered to the site via barge or tug and will be positioned within the same footprint as the previous float. The existing structure will be replaced with a new float constructed from standard, non-toxic materials, which, unlike in the present structure, will prevent continued deterioration.

Given the need for the float to support high load capacity during loading and unloading of passengers and cargo, and to ensure stability for public use in a wave-influenced environment, a complete subsurface floatation system is necessary. This results in 17% functional open space in this site's deepwater environment; this is the maximum functional open space that can be provided given the small size of the float and the safety and environmental conditions that influence final design.  
 
The float will connect to the six existing steel piles via five-sided pile hoops. Pile hoops will be connected by hand from a standing position on the new float or via a small support vessel accessing the pile hoops from 
beneath Pier 54.  
 
This project will occur overwater and will not require any in-water work. Removal of the existing float and installation of the new float is expected to be completed in 3 days or fewer.

properties.description:
The proposed project is to convert an existing 1 story, 5400sf mortuary building into the new home for the Rainier Valley Food Bank. 

The scope of work includes expanding and remodeling the existing building to allow food bank programs and operations to move in. Proposed spaces and alterations the design team is considering include: adding an interior or exterior walk-in cooler and a walk-in freezer; converting the existing lobby into a commercial kitchen with walk-up to-go window; adding a larger entry canopy; converting a large room into a grocery store-like distribution space; adding a small mezzanine; adding a loading dock; converting some existing parking spaces into a garden and waste enclosure; expand the building toward Rainier Ave by ~3900sf for additional office and staff support spaces.
There is also interest to activate and occupy the site with a temporary food village during the design, permitting, and construction process.

properties.description:
The proposed Pier 1 demolition and replacement activities include:

(1)Demolition of the existing Pier 1 timber and concrete structure.
(2)Installation of a commercial grade pier and an adjacent marina facility within the previous pier footprint. Activity is anticipated to include installation of a sheet pile wall within a portion of the aquatic habitat below the existing pier. Filling activities will occur behind the sheet pile wall to support installation of the new pier and marina facility.
(3)

Restoration of the existing shoreline revetment adjacent to the new pier and marina.
(4)Shoreline excavation to create area of gravel beach to compensate for unavoidable aquatic habitat impacts.






The existing pier consists of approximately 1,900 creosote piles and is significantly deteriorated with only a perimeter concrete apron that is in any measure of serviceable use. Replacement of the pier is needed to maintain the industrial/commercial marine use of the pier.

Based on soil and groundwater investigations, it is reported that upland soil, composed predominately of fill materials, is contaminated with metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

Restoration of the existing shoreline revetment is needed to prevent further erosion of the shoreline, and will assist in containing contaminated upland soils onsite.

Fill activities proposed below a portion of the existing pier's footprint, will partially utilize upland contaminated soils and suspected contaminated sediment (to the extent practicable) that will be disturbed during the course of  pier demolition and replacement activities and shoreline restoration. A sheet pile wall is proposed waterward of the area of fill to provide containment of the upland soil and dewatered sediment and protect the new pier structure. The new retaining wall feature will be contiguous with adjacent proposed shoreline revetment.
